serviceNotes: Dryer -Member stated the Samsung dryer is continuously running even when the unit is not in use and the control panel appears to be off. Based on the symptoms described, a likely cause is a stuck or welded motor relay on the main control board, which can continue supplying power to the drive motor even when no cycle has been selected. Other possible causes include a shorted control board, wiring issue, or less commonly a faulty user interface sending an unintended run command. Recommended diagnosis is to verify whether the motor continues running with the door open and to inspect the main control board for signs of relay failure, overheating, or burned components. If the motor relay is found to be stuck closed, replacement of the main control board will be required to restore normal operation 7/22/26 needs main control board-Mc DC97-21429B Control board 2 hours

Fridge quit cooling all together

1)
The ice maker in the door is making ice. The dispenser isn't
operating. So to get the ice out one must remove the ice maker from the
door and manually remove ice from the top.

2)
The new ice maker in the freezer made some huge ice cubes before we
arrived. Only used one. Noticed this morning that it was in the off
position, so I turned it on. In less than 5 minutes it started making
this loud banging sound so I turned it off. We won't use any more of the
7 big cubes in there.

3)
The error code is CF. From LG:

A CF error code indicates
that the feedback signal is less than 65 seconds during the fan's
operation. This refers to the fan at the back, bottom of the refrigerator that discharges heat from the
condenser.

Gate #6166 Door 9969

"Need dishwasher repair. The
flashing Normal light on your Samsung DW80CG4021SR likely means the
dishwasher is detecting a leak or moisture in the base pan. This triggers
flood mode, preventing cycles from running and causing the unit to power on
automatically. Shut off power and water to the unit. Pull the dishwasher out
from under the counter. Tip it forward to drain any water from the base pan.
Use towels or a shop vac to dry it thoroughly. Let the unit dry completely
before restoring power. Check the float or leak sensor for obstructions or
water. If the unit stops flashing and runs normally after drying, the issue
was likely minor moisture. If the flashing returns, inspect the water inlet
valve, hose connections, and pump seals for leaks. Replace the inlet valve if
it's faulty (a common cause of slow leaks). Once repairs are made, run a test
